target_customer: Independent accountants, accounting firms (despachos) and SMEs in Mexico
problem: Most Mexican accountants use desktop software designed decades ago and manually handle e-invoices (CFDI), reconciliation and tax filings for each client.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, flat monthly price per account
product_category: Cloud accounting and payroll automation for accountants

founders.name: Eduardo Williams
previous_startups: Consulting firm for ERP and CRM systems (with Carlos Salinas), outcome not stated
founders.background_notes: LatAm Fintech says he and Salinas met in Monterrey and began with an ERP and CRM consultancy before moving to accountants after the 2015 mandatory e-invoicing rule. No education or employers found.

founders.name: Carlos Salinas
previous_startups: Consulting firm for ERP and CRM systems (with Eduardo Williams), outcome not stated
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as cofounder and CTO; no education or employers found.

competitors.name: CONTPAQi
competitors.what: Desktop-first accounting suite widely used by Mexican accountants, with separate cloud products
competitors.traction_then: de facto standard among Mexican accounting firms

competitors.name: Aspel
competitors.what: Established Mexican accounting and ERP software
competitors.traction_then: listed among the most recognized accounting programs in Mexico

competitors.name: Alegra
competitors.what: Cloud accounting for Mexican SMEs and accountants
competitors.traction_then: cloud-first rival; figures for 2021 not found

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating CFDI downloads from the tax authority SAT, bank reconciliation, electronic accounting and payroll stamping for Mexican rules; standard SaaS with country-specific compliance work.

defensibility.rationale: Accountants keep client books in it and compliance logic is local, but competitors like Alegra and desktop incumbents' cloud versions target the same buyers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept desktop and cloud products alongside; no source shows Contalink copied or acquired.

market_need_then: Mandatory e-invoicing since 2015 created heavy volumes of CFDI to process; the CEO says about 80 percent of Mexican accountants still used desktop software designed decades ago.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and friendly, informal 'tu' in Spanish, benefit-focused lines such as 'Dile adios a consumir tu tiempo capturando datos', and a 'Hecho por mexicanos' identity claim.

brand_strength.rationale: Name fuses the Spanish word for accounting with link and is clear to the target market; the site claims over 25,000 accountants, but no press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.why: Mandatory e-invoicing in Mexico from 2015 shifted the founders toward serving accountants, per LatAm Fintech.

outcome_analysis: Contalink grew from an ERP consultancy into cloud accounting for Mexican accountants after e-invoicing rules created demand. By March 2022 it reported over 4,000 accountants managing 20,000 SMEs and a $2.1M round, and its site now claims over 25,000 accountants and a 75 person team. No later round, exit or shutdown was found; it appears a profitable-looking, steadily growing niche SaaS.
notes: Founding year conflicts (YC 2019, other sources 2014 or 2015). The LatAm Fintech page metadata tags the round as Debt Financing while the text says investment round; Forbes Mexico (dated 2022-03-15 per YC page) and VCBacked list it as seed. Competitor sources are from 2026 comparison pages; the facts used (CONTPAQi founded 1984, incumbent desktop status) predate the batch, but no 2021-dated source was found. Series A not found. No outcome news found for layoffs or acquisition.
